Question B-006-008-007.

Why the correct answer is right: In free space, radio waves are electromagnetic waves and travel at the speed of light. In materials such as coax dielectric they can be slower, but the Basic free-space reference is light speed.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "is constant": This is too absolute: propagation speed changes with the medium, such as a coaxial cable velocity factor, so it is not simply one constant in every situation.
- sourceIndex 2: "is less than half the speed of light": Free-space radio waves travel at light speed, not less than half of it; most ordinary feed-line velocity factors are also greater than one-half.
- sourceIndex 3: "varies depending on the frequency": In free space the speed is essentially independent of radio frequency; wavelength changes with frequency because wavelength equals speed divided by frequency.
